answer: Each epoch a central ledger issues a unique cryptographic signal that agents must reflect in a live inference mirror, proving they can solve a fresh reasoning puzzle tied to the current state of the network. The puzzle is generated from a random walk through a high‑dimensional canyon of model parameters, so reproducing it requires the attacker to run a full forward‑pass on a comparable AI model for every bogus identity. Thus a Sybil attack scales linearly with compute cost, turning a cheap identity flood into an expense equal to the combined inference budget of all legitimate agents.
